description: The NVMe cold tier below the host KV tier (docs/tp4-kv-nvme.md): a raw-namespace spill of the host tier's evictions and of the checkpoint store's, restored on a miss in both host stores, so a returning session's KV stays warm for up to a day since its last use (owner decisions 2026-10-21: all tenants, TTL 1 day) and comes back in about a second or two instead of a 75 to 145 s cold re-prefill. QWEN_PREFIX_NVME=1 with QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_DEVICE and the required QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_RETENTION_ACK=1, Write-through (QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_SPILL=through, idle 0) is the default and a graceful stop drains the writer queue (QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_DRAIN_S, default 4 s); the stored KV survives a deploy (the fingerprint is KV_EPOCH, the model, the drafter, the KV layout and three byte-defining switches, not the image or the profile name). The drive must be an Opal self-encrypting drive with locking enabled and unlocked (QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_REQUIRE_SED, on by default; 0 is a gate's own), TRIM is on by default. Never run on a card. The peer-to-peer restore (QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_P2P=1, a gate's name until a card has qualified it; docs/tp4-p2p-restore.md): the drive holds each block chip-major, the restore reads each card's share straight into its staging buffer through the published BAR4 window, checks it on the card against the checksum stored at spill and copies it into the cache with a device op, and falls back to the host backend on any failure.

smoke.what: NVMe cold tier below the host KV tier (the scheduler graft's install line; a REFUSED line, the zero-retention guard, logs no 'on' line and so fails the arm too)
the peer-to-peer restore (docs/tp4-p2p-restore.md): the cards' windows aimed and proved, the staging buffer allocated; a path that could not start logs UNAVAILABLE and the host backend serves

image_files.reason: the NVMe tier: flags, layout fingerprint, checkpoint codec, restore backends, the spill writer; qwen_prefix_registry and the contract import it only when a QWEN_PREFIX_NVME name is set
the raw-namespace object store under it: superblocks, journal, snapshots, extent allocator, O_DIRECT IO
the peer-to-peer restore's host side (window aim, p2pmem read, p2p_checksum, engine and stream); qwen_kv_nvme imports it only when QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_P2P=1

card_jobs: none written: docs/tp4-kv-nvme.md section 12 is the plan (D0 the drive bench, A1 the audited attach, N1 exactness at 64k/128k/254k, N2 timed restore, N3 spill under eight live seats, N4 the concurrent restore ABAB, N5 restart persistence, N6 write-through, E1 the encryption check, U1 the UPGRADE gate across two images, R1 the drive re-probe after a card reset that rescans PCI, Z the reset), and lists what the runner and the gate need first; the peer-to-peer restore's P3a is C2_FABRIC_PROBE=p2p (scripts/ci/references/tp4-p2p-jobs)
notes: FLAGS. All default off and strict (qwen_kv_nvme.parse); the switch needs the host tier, the device and QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_RETENTION_ACK=1. A traffic profile may name QWEN_PREFIX_NVME=1 only under an owner traffic waiver that names it (serving_c2_contract.NVME_WAIVABLE_LEVERS); the audit, the format override, the command directory and the zero-retention override stay a gate's. NO PROFILE TWIN YET: the gate arms are derived like the sliced restore's, and the plans are part of the gate work. The tier does not start (a REFUSED line, nvme_refused_zero_retention) on a node that looks zero-retention unless QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_ALLOW_ON_ZERO_RETENTION=1; a drive that cannot be opened logs UNAVAILABLE, and one that vanishes at run time logs DEVICE LOST once (nvme_device_lost); the host tier serves in both cases. The tier refuses to open a drive that is not shown to be encrypted (a REFUSED line, nvme_refused_not_encrypted); a gate profile sets QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_REQUIRE_SED=0 until the drive is set up.
